description:
Give the `query all` filter composition and gated readiness pure domain owners, so the CLI query suite can drop its remaining semantic cases.

## Background

`CommandExecutor::query_all` in `crates/jit/src/commands/query.rs` composes the state, assignee, priority and label filters itself, by successive `retain` calls in the command layer. No pure domain function or domain test owns that AND-composition, so the CLI suite `crates/jit/tests/cli_query_graph/query_tests.rs` still holds three combined-filter cases (state with priority, state with assignee, state with label) as its only proof of it. The same suite holds the only proof that an issue in `Ready` whose required gates have not passed still appears in `query_ready` (gates gate completion, not start). The domain owners for the other query properties live in `crates/jit/src/domain/queries.rs`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One pure function in `crates/jit/src/domain/queries.rs` applies the `query all` filters (state, assignee, priority, labels) as a conjunction over a slice of issues, and `query_all` applies its result without filtering issues itself.
- [hard] REQ-02: Unit tests in `domain/queries.rs` own the conjunction of each filter with each other filter, and a property-based test shows the result is exactly the issues every supplied filter admits.
- [hard] REQ-03: A unit test in `domain/queries.rs` owns that an unassigned, unblocked `Ready` issue with unpassed required gates is in `query_ready`'s result.
- [hard] REQ-04: `query all` output and exit status are unchanged for every filter combination.
title: Domain owners for query-all filter composition and gated readiness
